- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# ROADMAP: gem5 CPU-Switch Parity
2	
3	Tracks 22 independent features to extend hybrid_sim (QEMU + vsim) with the four
4	CPU-switch mechanisms from `specs/hybrid-sim-gem5-switch-parity.md`. F1-F12
5	are the gem5-parity core (CSR/PC/icount/SimPoint switching); F13-F22 add
6	gem5-style `--vsim-warmup-icount` so the reported cycle figure excludes the
7	vsim cold-cache prefix. One session = one feature. Update status when
8	starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
9	
10	## Status Legend
11	
12	- not-started: feature has not begun
13	- in-progress: currently being implemented in a session
14	- done: behavioural+structural commits landed and tests pass
15	
16	## Dependency DAG
17	
18	```
19	F1 ----+----> F4
20	F2 ----+
21	F3 ----+
22	F5 ----+----> F6
23	       +----> F7 ----> F12 ----> F11
24	       +----> F8 ----> F9 ----> F10
25	
26	F13 (ABI) --+--> F14 (snapshot) --+--> F15 (vsim CLI) --+--> F17 (e2e CSR)
27	            |                     |                     +--> F18 (e2e PC)
28	            +-----> F16 (drain) --+                     +--> F19 (e2e icount, also needs F5,F6)
29	                                  |
30	                                  +--> F20 (orchestrator)  +--> F22 (docs; needs F17..F21)
31	                                                           +
32	F15 ----------------------------> F21 (hsim driver) -------+
33	```
34	
35	Migration order: ship F1, F2, F3 first (infrastructure layer). After that,
36	F5/F6/F7 parallelise across sessions because they touch independent files.
37	F12 (SimPoint binary integration) sits between BBV emission (F7) and
38	slice-consume (F11) because F11's slice indices come from SimPoint's
39	clustering output.
40	
41	Warmup wave (F13-F22) runs after F1-F12. F13 is the load-bearing structural
42	gate; F14-F16 are the three independent leaf landings on top of it; F17-F21
43	parallelise across sessions; F22 closes the wave once green.
44	
45	## Features
46	
47	### F1 - Rebrand plugin drain-exit code 0 -> 200
48	
49	- Status: done
50	- Type: structural
51	- Description: Today `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:261` exits 0 on drain;
52	  workload completion and drain are indistinguishable. vsim already exits
53	  200 (`verilator/src/hybrid/exit_codes.hpp:7`). Bring the plugin in
54	  line. The orchestrator (F2+) relies on this distinction.
55	- Key files:
56	  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:261`
57	  - `tests/e2e.sh` (exit-code assertions)
58	  - `tests/e2e.sh`
59	- Dependencies: none
60	- TDD RED: a test in `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_drain_exit_code.sh` runs
61	  the plugin with a CSR fixture and asserts QEMU exits with code 200.
62	  Fails on today's 0.
63	
64	### F2 - Orchestrator skeleton (Python package)
65	
66	- Status: done
67	- Type: structural (new code)
68	- Description: Create `tools/orchestrator/` Python package. CLI parsing,
69	  plan loading from YAML, dry-run that prints the planned spawns. No real
70	  spawn yet.
71	- Key files:
72	  - `tools/orchestrator/__init__.py` (new)
73	  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py` (new)
74	  - `tools/orchestrator/plan.py` (new)
75	  - `tools/orchestrator/examples/csr_oneshot.yaml` (new)
76	- Dependencies: none
77	- TDD RED: `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_plan_parses.py` loads
78	  `examples/csr_oneshot.yaml` and asserts the resulting `Session` has
79	  three `Step` entries. Fails because no parser exists.

81	### F3 - ctypes ABI binding + state-file validator
82	
83	- Status: done
84	- Type: structural (new code)
85	- Description: Mirror `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`'s `hybrid_state_v1` in
86	  Python via ctypes. Field-offset asserts at import time. Add
87	  `validate_state_file(path)` checking magic 0x42594841, version 1,
88	  exact `sizeof(hybrid_state_v1)` bytes. Wire into orchestrator as the
89	  post-spawn gate.

96	  `hybrid_state_v1` struct from a small C harness, reads it in Python,

98	  ctypes layout matches C.

100	### F4 - Orchestrator runs today's CSR fixture end-to-end
101	
102	- Status: done. The in-process spawn at `main.cpp:478-490` (later
103	  renumbered to `:530-542`) was removed in the F4-cleanup pass: see
104	  `f4_cleanup.md`. `tests/e2e.sh` now invokes
105	  `python3 -m orchestrator.main qemu-resume` for the QEMU2 leg;
106	  `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`, its doctest, and the obsolete
107	  `rt_no_qemu_binary` / `rt_gdbstub_timeout` / `rt_pty_handback` drivers
108	  are deleted. Python gdbstub remains the canonical state-restore path.
109	- Type: behavioral
110	- Description: Replace one `e2e.sh` invocation with
111	  `orchestrator run <yaml>` for `rt_c_v_regs`. Add the C++ helper
112	  `tools/hybrid_apply_state` extracted from `qemu_handback.hpp`'s
113	  state-restore body. Delete the in-process spawn at `main.cpp:478-490`;
114	  vsim returns 200 cleanly.
115	- Key files:
116	  - `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` (new)
117	  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py`
118	  - `tools/hybrid_apply_state/` (new C++ CLI; lifts from
119	    `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp:287-335 apply_state`,
120	    `:41-63 pick_free_port`)
121	  - `verilator/src/main.cpp:478-490` (delete)
122	  - `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake:108-238` (add CTest variant)
123	- Dependencies: F1, F2, F3
124	- TDD RED: `ctest -R rt_c_v_regs--orchestrator` is registered but the
125	  orchestrator's spawn path is incomplete; test fails. Then asserts

128	### F5 - icount counter + trigger in QEMU plugin
129	
130	- Status: done. Trigger priority (spec section 5 row 1: CSR/PC > BBV >
131	  icount) is deferred - F5 registers icount tick FIRST in
132	  `vcpu_tb_trans`, so it wins on insns where both fire. The F5 e2e uses
133	  a CSR-less fixture, so this is invisible today; F11 (slice-consume)
134	  will revisit when BBV ties enter the picture.
135	- Type: behavioral
136	- Description: Add `uint64_t icount_retired` incremented in a per-insn
137	  callback registered alongside the CSR/PC matcher in
138	  `vcpu_tb_trans()`. New plugin arg `icount=N`. When
139	  `icount_retired >= icount_target`, set the should-exit flag and call
140	  `on_handoff` at the same insn boundary.
141	- Key files:
142	  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:264-300` (`vcpu_tb_trans`)
143	  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:302-339` (arg parser)
144	- Dependencies: F1
145	- TDD RED: `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_icount_trigger.sh` runs a fixture
146	  with `--plugin-args icount=100000` on a CSR-less binary; asserts the
147	  drained state file's `minstret >= 100000` and exit code is 200. Fails
148	  because the `icount=` arg is unknown.

150	### F6 - vsim IcountTrigger (sibling of CsrTrigger)
151	
152	- Status: done. `HandoffController` was retrofitted to a class template
153	  on the trigger type (structural; CTAD preserves all existing call
154	  sites). `IcountTrigger` lives at `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp`
155	  with the duck-type surface (`lookup`, `empty`, `observe_commit`).
156	  `--hybrid-icount N` is wired in `main.cpp` and dispatches into
157	  `Simulator::enable_hybrid_icount_handoff`. Mutually exclusive with
158	  `--hybrid-exit-pc`. Unit test
159	  `tests/hybrid/icount_trigger.test.cpp` covers both the standalone
160	  trigger and the templated controller's drain.
161	- Type: behavioral
162	- Description: New `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp` with the
163	  same duck-type surface as `CsrTrigger` (`lookup(pc) ->
164	  std::optional<hit>`, plus an `observe_commit()` that increments the
165	  per-hart counter). `HandoffController` is already template-parameterised
166	  on trigger type (`handoff_controller.hpp:38`). Add
167	  `--hybrid-icount N` to `main.cpp:466-472`. Multi-hart out of scope
168	  (plan-validation rejects `hart_id != 0`).
169	- Key files:
170	  - `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp` (new)
171	  - `verilator/src/main.cpp:466-472`
172	  - `verilator/src/simulator.hpp:223-253` (registration)
173	- Dependencies: none (parallel to F5)
174	- TDD RED: `verilator/tests/hybrid/test_icount_trigger.cpp` (doctest)

176	  ticks, asserts `on_retire` returns a drained state at exactly the
177	  100th. Fails because the class does not exist.

179	### F7 - BBV emission plugin (profile mode)
180	
181	- Status: done. `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.{c,h}` provides a self-contained
182	  SimPoint-format emitter (PC -> bb_id hash, per-slice flush, sparse
183	  rows matching the SimPoint 3.2 sample.bb convention). Plugin args
184	  `bbv_out=PATH,slice=N` register a per-insn callback that ticks the
185	  emitter; it is registered BEFORE the icount callback so when both
186	  fire on the same insn (icount target == slice multiple) the slice
187	  row is durable before exit(200). The shipped SimPoint binary
188	  (F12) parses the emitted file without error. Verified end-to-end:
189	  on icount_spin with ICOUNT=1M,SLICE=10k, SimPoint identifies 2
190	  phases (startup weight 0.01, steady-state loop weight 0.99) which
191	  matches the workload's structure.
192	- Type: behavioral
193	- Description: BBV emission as a second sub-mode of `hybrid_handoff`
194	  (not a separate plugin - keeps per-insn callback cost to one
195	  per insn). New plugin args `bbv_out=PATH,slice=N`. Emit one BBV row
196	  per `slice` dynamic insns into a SimPoint-readable `.bb` file.
197	- Key files:
198	  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`
199	  - `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.c` (new sub-module)
200	  - `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.h` (new)
201	  - `qemu_plugin/Makefile`
202	  - `tests/plugin/test_plugin_bbv_emit.sh` (new)
203	- Dependencies: F5 (reuses the per-insn callback path)
204	- TDD RED: `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_bbv_emit.sh` runs icount_spin
205	  with `bbv_out=/tmp/x.bb,slice=1000,icount=10000`; asserts the file
206	  has exactly 10 SimPoint-format rows and the SimPoint binary parses
207	  it. Failed pre-implementation because the plugin rejected
208	  `bbv_out=` as an unknown option.
209	
210	### F8 - Orchestrator N-way switching with YAML plan grammar
211	
212	- Status: done
213	- Type: behavioral
214	- Description: Parse the full `steps:` grammar. Implement the spawn
215	  loop: spawn, wait, validate state file, archive (no-op if no
216	  `archive_as`), advance. Pass `--state-in` from previous spawn's
217	  `--state-out`. Mmap fd held open across all spawns.
218	- As built: `runner.run_session()` iterates `session.steps`, dispatching
219	  per `(model, trigger.kind)` to `_qemu_drain`, `_vsim_drain`, or
220	  `_qemu_resume_to_end`. The session-wide /dev/shm fd lives in
221	  `MmapOwner` (RAII context manager). `run_session()` now returns a
222	  `SessionResult(exit_code, state_paths)`; `state_paths` lists every
223	  drain-step's persisted state file. CLI gains `--workdir DIR` so
224	  callers can keep intermediate state for inspection (F9 will hook
225	  the archive copy here). `step.archive_as` is accepted but ignored
226	  in F8 - F9 will consume it.
227	- Key files:
228	  - `tools/orchestrator/runner.py` (rewrite: N-step loop + SessionResult)
229	  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py` (CLI `--workdir`, SessionResult unpack)
230	  - `tools/orchestrator/mmap_owner.py` (new RAII module)
231	  - `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_mmap_owner.py` (new unit tests)
232	  - `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_two_step_session.py` (new RED test)
233	- Dependencies: F4
234	- TDD RED: `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_two_step_session.py` runs a
235	  2-step drain plan (QEMU drain on CSR enter, vsim drain on CSR exit)
236	  on `rt_c_v_regs`; asserts the runner accepts `work_dir=` and
237	  returns a `SessionResult` whose two `state_paths` each pass
238	  `validate_state_file()`. RED today: `run_session()` rejects
239	  `work_dir=` kwarg and is hard-coded to 3 steps.

241	### F9 - Checkpoint archive write
242	
243	- Status: done
244	- Type: behavioral
245	- Description: When a step has `archive_as: snap/N`, after the spawn
246	  exits, copy `state.bin` and the mmap into `snap/N/`; write
247	  `meta.json`. Reflink-or-copy by filesystem probe (btrfs/xfs use
248	  `cp --reflink=always`; ext4 falls back to sequential `cp`).
249	- As built: `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py::write_archive()` is the
250	  self-contained primitive that serialises `state.bin` (shutil.copy),
251	  `mem` (`cp --reflink=auto` with shutil fallback), and `meta.json`
252	  (schema=1; carries abi_version, abi_magic, flags, vlen_bytes,
253	  mem_size, elf_path, source_step_index, captured_at, plus optional
254	  cpu_variant/region_id/slice_index for F10's replay validation).
255	  `runner.run_session()` gained an `archive_root` kwarg (defaults to
256	  `project_root`) and invokes `write_archive` after `validate_state_file`
257	  when `step.archive_as` is set. cpu_variant is inferred from the vsim
258	  binary name (`sim_<variant>`); slice_index is parsed from the
259	  trailing path component when numeric. CLI exposes `--archive-root`.
260	- Key files:
261	  - `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py` (new)
262	  - `tools/orchestrator/runner.py` (archive hook + cpu_variant/slice_index helpers)
263	  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py` (`--archive-root` flag)
264	  - `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_checkpoint.py` (new unit tests)
265	  - `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_checkpoint_archive.py` (new e2e RED test)
266	- Dependencies: F8
267	- TDD RED:
268	  `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_checkpoint_archive.py` runs a 1-step
269	  plan with `archive_as: snap/0`; asserts the three artefacts exist
270	  and `state.bin` byte-matches the in-flight one.
271	
272	### F10 - Checkpoint replay (`replay-checkpoint <dir>`)
273	
274	- Status: done
275	- Type: behavioral
276	- Description: New orchestrator entry point. Validates `meta.json`
277	  against the live binary's CPU variant and VLEN. Hydrates a new
278	  `/dev/shm` mmap from `snap/N/mem`. Copies `state.bin` to working
279	  path. Spawns the requested model. No plugin or vsim code change.
280	- As built: `checkpoint.replay_checkpoint(snap_dir, model, ...)` is
281	  the Python entry. It loads `meta.json`, invokes
282	  `validate_replay_meta()` (F10 structural primitive: rejects schema/
283	  abi_version/abi_magic/cpu_variant/vlen_bytes mismatches up-front),
284	  copies `state.bin` into `work_dir/replay-state-in.bin`, allocates a
285	  fresh `/dev/shm` mmap via `MmapOwner.allocate(mem_size)`, overwrites
286	  it with `snap/N/mem`, and synthesises a 1-step `Session`
287	  (`(vsim, csr)` or `(qemu, end_of_program)`) handed to
288	  `run_session()` with the new `initial_state_in=` kwarg. CLI exposes
289	  `orchestrator replay-checkpoint <snap_dir> --resume-with
290	  {vsim,qemu} [--project-root R] [--workdir W]`. Final assertion was
291	  weakened from "GPRs match" to "PC differs + bytes differ + flags/
292	  vlenb match"; minstret on andes-ax45mpv is not a reliable per-spawn
293	  counter on either QEMU plugin or vsim drain.
294	- Key files:
295	  - `tools/orchestrator/checkpoint.py` (`validate_replay_meta`,
296	    `replay_checkpoint`, `LIVE_VLEN_BYTES`)
297	  - `tools/orchestrator/runner.py` (`initial_state_in` kwarg)
298	  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py` (`replay-checkpoint` subcommand)
299	  - `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_checkpoint.py` (validator units)
300	  - `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_checkpoint_replay.py` (e2e RED test)
301	- Dependencies: F9
302	- TDD RED:
303	  `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_checkpoint_replay.py` writes a known
304	  archive (using F9), runs `replay-checkpoint snap/0 --resume-with
305	  vsim`; asserts the spawned vsim drains a state file whose GPRs
306	  match the archive.
307	
308	### F11 - BBV slice-consume trigger
309	
310	- Status: done. Plugin args `slice=N,slice_at=K` add a third sub-mode
311	  to `hybrid_handoff` (alongside CSR/PC, icount, BBV-emit). A
312	  per-insn callback counts retired insns into a slice accumulator;
313	  on every Nth insn the slice index advances. When the slice index
314	  exceeds the target `slice_at=K` (0-based), drain fires via the
315	  same `on_handoff` path. Reuses the existing `slice=` parameter so
316	  BBV-emit and slice-consume share one source of truth for slice
317	  size. Plugin emits a deterministic `idx=K+1 target=K` stderr line
318	  at drain so the e2e test can verify timing without relying on
319	  `minstret` (which is a cycle-counter proxy on andes-ax45mpv).
320	  Orchestrator-side `phase` trigger kind in `plan.py` is deferred
321	  to the F8 N-way wave -- F11's plugin contract stands alone and
322	  the test invokes the plugin directly with `slice=N,slice_at=K`.
323	- Type: behavioral
324	- Description: Third sub-mode of `hybrid_handoff` (after CSR/PC,

# ROADMAP: gem5 CPU-Switch Parity

Tracks 22 independent features to extend hybrid_sim (QEMU + vsim) with the four
CPU-switch mechanisms from `specs/hybrid-sim-gem5-switch-parity.md`. F1-F12
are the gem5-parity core (CSR/PC/icount/SimPoint switching); F13-F22 add
gem5-style `--vsim-warmup-icount` so the reported cycle figure excludes the
vsim cold-cache prefix. One session = one feature. Update status when
starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).

## Status Legend

- not-started: feature has not begun
- in-progress: currently being implemented in a session
- done: behavioural+structural commits landed and tests pass

## Dependency DAG

```
F1 ----+----> F4
F2 ----+
F3 ----+
F5 ----+----> F6
       +----> F7 ----> F12 ----> F11
       +----> F8 ----> F9 ----> F10

F13 (ABI) --+--> F14 (snapshot) --+--> F15 (vsim CLI) --+--> F17 (e2e CSR)
            |                     |                     +--> F18 (e2e PC)
            +-----> F16 (drain) --+                     +--> F19 (e2e icount, also needs F5,F6)
                                  |
                                  +--> F20 (orchestrator)  +--> F22 (docs; needs F17..F21)
                                                           +
F15 ----------------------------> F21 (hsim driver) -------+
```

Migration order: ship F1, F2, F3 first (infrastructure layer). After that,
F5/F6/F7 parallelise across sessions because they touch independent files.
F12 (SimPoint binary integration) sits between BBV emission (F7) and
slice-consume (F11) because F11's slice indices come from SimPoint's
clustering output.

Warmup wave (F13-F22) runs after F1-F12. F13 is the load-bearing structural
gate; F14-F16 are the three independent leaf landings on top of it; F17-F21
parallelise across sessions; F22 closes the wave once green.

## Features

### F1 - Rebrand plugin drain-exit code 0 -> 200

- Status: done
- Type: structural
- Description: Today `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:261` exits 0 on drain;
  workload completion and drain are indistinguishable. vsim already exits
  200 (`verilator/src/hybrid/exit_codes.hpp:7`). Bring the plugin in
  line. The orchestrator (F2+) relies on this distinction.
- Key files:
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:261`
  - `tests/e2e.sh` (exit-code assertions)
  - `tests/e2e.sh`
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: a test in `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_drain_exit_code.sh` runs
  the plugin with a CSR fixture and asserts QEMU exits with code 200.
  Fails on today's 0.

### F2 - Orchestrator skeleton (Python package)

- Status: done
- Type: structural (new code)
- Description: Create `tools/orchestrator/` Python package. CLI parsing,
  plan loading from YAML, dry-run that prints the planned spawns. No real
  spawn yet.
- Key files:
  - `tools/orchestrator/__init__.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/plan.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/examples/csr_oneshot.yaml` (new)
- Dependencies: none
- TDD RED: `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_plan_parses.py` loads
  `examples/csr_oneshot.yaml` and asserts the resulting `Session` has
  three `Step` entries. Fails because no parser exists.

### F3 - ctypes ABI binding + state-file validator

- Status: done
- Type: structural (new code)
- Description: Mirror `include/hybrid/state_abi.h`'s `hybrid_state_v1` in
  Python via ctypes. Field-offset asserts at import time. Add
  `validate_state_file(path)` checking magic 0x42594841, version 1,
  exact `sizeof(hybrid_state_v1)` bytes. Wire into orchestrator as the
  post-spawn gate.
- Key files:
  - `tools/orchestrator/abi.py` (new)
  - `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (read-only)
  - `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h` (read-only; mirror its asserts)
- Dependencies: F2
- TDD RED: `tools/orchestrator/tests/test_abi_roundtrip.py` writes a known
  `hybrid_state_v1` struct from a small C harness, reads it in Python,
  asserts all fields (GPRs, FPRs, CSRs, V-state) match. Fails until
  ctypes layout matches C.

### F4 - Orchestrator runs today's CSR fixture end-to-end

- Status: done. The in-process spawn at `main.cpp:478-490` (later
  renumbered to `:530-542`) was removed in the F4-cleanup pass: see
  `f4_cleanup.md`. `tests/e2e.sh` now invokes
  `python3 -m orchestrator.main qemu-resume` for the QEMU2 leg;
  `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp`, its doctest, and the obsolete
  `rt_no_qemu_binary` / `rt_gdbstub_timeout` / `rt_pty_handback` drivers
  are deleted. Python gdbstub remains the canonical state-restore path.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: Replace one `e2e.sh` invocation with
  `orchestrator run <yaml>` for `rt_c_v_regs`. Add the C++ helper
  `tools/hybrid_apply_state` extracted from `qemu_handback.hpp`'s
  state-restore body. Delete the in-process spawn at `main.cpp:478-490`;
  vsim returns 200 cleanly.
- Key files:
  - `tools/orchestrator/spawn.py` (new)
  - `tools/orchestrator/main.py`
  - `tools/hybrid_apply_state/` (new C++ CLI; lifts from
    `verilator/src/hybrid/qemu_handback.hpp:287-335 apply_state`,
    `:41-63 pick_free_port`)
  - `verilator/src/main.cpp:478-490` (delete)
  - `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake:108-238` (add CTest variant)
- Dependencies: F1, F2, F3
- TDD RED: `ctest -R rt_c_v_regs--orchestrator` is registered but the
  orchestrator's spawn path is incomplete; test fails. Then asserts
  exit-code parity with `rt_c_v_regs--csr` (the bash-harness version).

### F5 - icount counter + trigger in QEMU plugin

- Status: done. Trigger priority (spec section 5 row 1: CSR/PC > BBV >
  icount) is deferred - F5 registers icount tick FIRST in
  `vcpu_tb_trans`, so it wins on insns where both fire. The F5 e2e uses
  a CSR-less fixture, so this is invisible today; F11 (slice-consume)
  will revisit when BBV ties enter the picture.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: Add `uint64_t icount_retired` incremented in a per-insn
  callback registered alongside the CSR/PC matcher in
  `vcpu_tb_trans()`. New plugin arg `icount=N`. When
  `icount_retired >= icount_target`, set the should-exit flag and call
  `on_handoff` at the same insn boundary.
- Key files:
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:264-300` (`vcpu_tb_trans`)
  - `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:302-339` (arg parser)
- Dependencies: F1
- TDD RED: `tests/hybrid/test_plugin_icount_trigger.sh` runs a fixture
  with `--plugin-args icount=100000` on a CSR-less binary; asserts the
  drained state file's `minstret >= 100000` and exit code is 200. Fails
  because the `icount=` arg is unknown.

### F6 - vsim IcountTrigger (sibling of CsrTrigger)

- Status: done. `HandoffController` was retrofitted to a class template
  on the trigger type (structural; CTAD preserves all existing call
  sites). `IcountTrigger` lives at `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp`
  with the duck-type surface (`lookup`, `empty`, `observe_commit`).
  `--hybrid-icount N` is wired in `main.cpp` and dispatches into
  `Simulator::enable_hybrid_icount_handoff`. Mutually exclusive with
  `--hybrid-exit-pc`. Unit test
  `tests/hybrid/icount_trigger.test.cpp` covers both the standalone
  trigger and the templated controller's drain.
- Type: behavioral
- Description: New `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp` with the
  same duck-type surface as `CsrTrigger` (`lookup(pc) ->
  std::optional<hit>`, plus an `observe_commit()` that increments the
  per-hart counter). `HandoffController` is already template-parameterised
  on trigger type (`handoff_controller.hpp:38`). Add
  `--hybrid-icount N` to `main.cpp:466-472`. Multi-hart out of scope
  (plan-validation rejects `hart_id != 0`).
- Key files:
  - `verilator/src/hybrid/icount_trigger.hpp` (new)
  - `verilator/src/main.cpp:466-472`
  - `verilator/src/simulator.hpp:223-253` (registration)
- Dependencies: none (parallel to F5)
- TDD RED: `verilator/tests/hybrid/test_icount_trigger.cpp` (doctest)
  builds a `RecordingBus` + `IcountTrigger(N=100)`, drives 100 retire
  ticks, asserts `on_retire` returns a drained state at exactly the
  100th. Fails because the class does not exist.

### F7 - BBV emission plugin (profile mode)

- Status: done. `qemu_plugin/bbv_emit.{c,h}` provides a self-contained
  SimPoint-format emitter (PC -> bb_id hash, per-slice flush, sparse

# Warm-up in hsim - simple version

## The problem
Today vsim reports cycles for the whole ROI. But when vsim starts, caches/BPU/TLB are cold, so the first chunk of cycles is artificially slow. The number is biased.

gem5 fixes this with `--warmup-insts N` + `m5.stats.reset()`. hsim can't copy this directly because QEMU has no cache model -- warm-up must happen INSIDE vsim.

## The idea
Don't restart the counter. Just remember where it was K insns after vsim entry. Then `measure_cycles = final_mcycle - mcycle_at_measure_start`.

```
vsim entry                K-th insn               drain
   |                         |                      |
   |--- warmup (cold) -------|--- measure (warm) ---|
   ^                         ^                      ^
   mcycle_start              snapshot               mcycle_end

measure_cycles = mcycle_end - snapshot
warmup_cycles  = snapshot   - mcycle_start
total_cycles   = mcycle_end - mcycle_start
```

Cache stays warm because vsim is one process -- only the stats window moves.

## How to wire it (F13-F22 in roadmap)

1. **ABI** (F13): add two `uint64_t` to `hybrid_state_v1` -- `mcycle_at_measure_start`, `minstret_at_measure_start`. Reuse bytes from `reserved[232]`, so wire size stays the same.
2. **vsim observer** (F14): new `measure_start_snapshot.hpp`, same duck-type shape as `IcountTrigger`. On the K-th `observe_commit()`, read `mcycle`/`minstret` via DMI and stash.
3. **vsim CLI** (F15): `--vsim-warmup-icount K` in `main.cpp`. K=0 disables (no DMI traffic, fields stay 0).
4. **Drain** (F16): `state_drain.hpp` copies the stashed values into the new ABI fields. ResumeDriver does NOT restore them -- drain-only metadata.
5. **e2e** (F17/F18/F19): one test per mode (csr/pc/icount), assert `0 < snapshot < final`.
6. **Orchestrator** (F20): read the two fields, print 3-way breakdown (warmup/measure/total). Ship `measure_cycles` as the ROI figure.
7. **hsim driver** (F21): forward `--vsim-warmup-icount` from `./hsim run` to the orchestrator's vsim step.
8. **Docs** (F22): delete the "cold cache included" caveat in USER_GUIDE + tutorial, add a "Warmup window" section.

## Key contract
- K=0 -> behaviour bit-identical to today; snapshot fields stay 0.
- K>0 but workload exits inside warmup window -> fields stay 0 (orchestrator prints "warmup: disabled").
- The mechanism is mode-agnostic: it counts vsim retired commits, not trigger source. csr/pc/icount/simpoint all use the same K.
I'll read the ABI files first to understand the current layout, then update roadmap status and start TDD.

"""Python ctypes mirror of `include/hybrid/state_abi.h::hybrid_state_v1`.

The C ABI is the wire contract between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the
orchestrator. This module mirrors it in ctypes so the orchestrator can
read and validate state files written by either CPU model.

Field offsets and the total struct size are asserted at import time
against the constants codified in `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`.
If a future ABI change forgets to update one side, importing this
module fails loudly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import struct
from pathlib import Path

HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC: int = 0x42594841
HYBRID_STATE_VERSION: int = 1

HYBRID_FLAG_RV64: int = 1 << 0
HYBRID_FLAG_FP: int = 1 << 1
HYBRID_FLAG_V: int = 1 << 2

HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: int = 64
HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM: int = 16
HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM: int = 64


class HybridStateV1(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("magic", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("version", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("flags", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("hart_id", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("pc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("priv", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("gpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("fpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("mstatus", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mepc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtvec", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcause", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtval", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mscratch", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("medeleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mideleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mip", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mie", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcycle", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("minstret", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("satp", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("pmpcfg", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM),
        ("pmpaddr", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM),
        ("vstart", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vtype", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vl", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vlenb", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vreg", ctypes.c_uint8 * (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)),
        ("vxsat", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vxrm", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vcsr", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("reserved", ctypes.c_uint8 * 232),
    ]


HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE: int = ctypes.sizeof(HybridStateV1)


# Mirror state_abi_check.h. If any of these fire, the ctypes layout has
# drifted from C and the wire format would be silently mis-parsed.
def _check_layout() -> None:
    expected: dict[str, int] = {
        "magic": 0,
        "version": 4,
        "flags": 8,
        "hart_id": 12,
        "pc": 16,
        "priv": 24,
        "gpr": 32,
        "fpr": 288,
        "mstatus": 544,
        "mepc": 552,
        "mtvec": 560,
        "mcause": 568,
        "mtval": 576,
        "mscratch": 584,
        "medeleg": 592,
        "mideleg": 600,
        "mip": 608,
        "mie": 616,
        "mcycle": 624,
        "minstret": 632,
        "satp": 640,
        "pmpcfg": 648,
        "pmpaddr": 776,
        "vstart": 1288,
        "vtype": 1296,
        "vl": 1304,
        "vlenb": 1312,
        "vreg": 1320,
    }
    vreg_end = 1320 + 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX
    expected["vxsat"] = vreg_end
    expected["vxrm"] = vreg_end + 8
    expected["vcsr"] = vreg_end + 16
    expected["reserved"] = vreg_end + 24
    for name, want in expected.items():
        got = getattr(HybridStateV1, name).offset
        if got != want:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"hybrid_state_v1.{name} offset mismatch: C={want} ctypes={got}"
            )
    want_size = vreg_end + 256
    if HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE != want_size:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"sizeof(hybrid_state_v1) mismatch: "
            f"C={want_size} ctypes={HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE}"
        )


_check_layout()


def validate_state_file(path: str | Path) -> None:
    """Raise ValueError if `path` is not a valid v1 hybrid state file.

    Checks (in order):
      - file size equals `sizeof(hybrid_state_v1)`
      - magic header equals `HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC`
      - version equals `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`

    Does not validate field semantics (e.g. flag bit consistency, PC
    sanity); that is the consumer's responsibility.
    """
    p = Path(path)
    raw = p.read_bytes()
    if len(raw) != HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{p}: size {len(raw)} != expected {HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE}"
        )
    magic, version = struct.unpack_from("<II", raw, 0)
    if magic != HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{p}: magic 0x{magic:08x} != expected 0x{HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC:08x}"
        )
    if version != HYBRID_STATE_VERSION:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{p}: version {version} != expected {HYBRID_STATE_VERSION}"
        )

1	"""F3 RED: Python ctypes mirror of `hybrid_state_v1` round-trips with C.
2	
3	A small C harness writes a `hybrid_state_v1` with known values. The Python
4	ctypes mirror reads it back and asserts every field block (header, GPRs,
5	FPRs, M-mode CSRs, PMP, V-state) byte-matches what C wrote. If any offset
6	or width drifts, the ctypes layout has fallen out of sync with the wire
7	format and the orchestrator will silently mis-parse state files.
8	
9	Also exercises `validate_state_file` on a good file plus two malformed
10	inputs (bad magic, wrong size).
11	"""
12	from __future__ import annotations
13	
14	import shutil
15	import subprocess
16	from pathlib import Path
17	
18	import pytest
19	
20	from orchestrator.abi import (
21	    HYBRID_FLAG_FP,
22	    HYBRID_FLAG_RV64,
23	    HYBRID_FLAG_V,
24	    HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM,
25	    HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM,
26	    HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC,
27	    HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE,
28	    HYBRID_STATE_VERSION,
29	    HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX,
30	    HybridStateV1,
31	    validate_state_file,
32	)
33	
34	_PROJECT_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
35	_INCLUDE_DIR = _PROJECT_ROOT / "include"
36	
37	_C_HARNESS = r"""
38	#include <stdio.h>
39	#include <stdlib.h>
40	#include <string.h>
41	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
42	
43	int main(int argc, char** argv) {
44	    if (argc != 2) return 1;
45	    struct hybrid_state_v1 s;
46	    memset(&s, 0, sizeof(s));
47	    s.magic = HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC;
48	    s.version = HYBRID_STATE_VERSION;
49	    s.flags = HYBRID_FLAG_RV64 | HYBRID_FLAG_FP | HYBRID_FLAG_V;
50	    s.hart_id = 0;
51	    s.pc = 0x80000000ULL;
52	    s.priv = 3;
53	    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) s.gpr[i] = 0x1000ULL + (uint64_t)i;
54	    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) s.fpr[i] = 0x2000ULL + (uint64_t)i;
55	    s.mstatus  = 0xabcdef01ULL;
56	    s.mepc     = 0xdeadbeefULL;
57	    s.mtvec    = 0x80000040ULL;
58	    s.mcause   = 7;
59	    s.mtval    = 0x1234;
60	    s.mscratch = 0x5678;
61	    s.mcycle   = 1000;
62	    s.minstret = 500;
63	    for (int i = 0; i < HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM;  i++) s.pmpcfg[i]  = 0x10ULL + (uint64_t)i;
64	    for (int i = 0; i < HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM; i++) s.pmpaddr[i] = 0x100ULL + (uint64_t)i;
65	    s.vstart = 0;
66	    s.vtype  = 0xdaULL;
67	    s.vl     = 16;
68	    s.vlenb  = HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX;
69	    for (int i = 0; i < 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX; i++) {
70	        s.vreg[i] = (uint8_t)(i & 0xff);
71	    }
72	    s.vxsat = 1;
73	    s.vxrm  = 2;
74	    s.vcsr  = 3;
75	    FILE* f = fopen(argv[1], "wb");
76	    if (!f) return 2;
77	    if (fwrite(&s, sizeof(s), 1, f) != 1) { fclose(f); return 3; }
78	    fclose(f);
79	    return 0;
80	}
81	"""
82	
83	
84	def _cc() -> str:
85	    cc = shutil.which("cc") or shutil.which("gcc") or shutil.which("clang")
86	    if cc is None:
87	        pytest.skip("no C compiler available")
88	    return cc
89	
90	
91	@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
92	def known_state_bin(tmp_path_factory) -> Path:
93	    work = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("abi_harness")
94	    c_path = work / "harness.c"
95	    bin_path = work / "harness"
96	    out_path = work / "state.bin"
97	    c_path.write_text(_C_HARNESS)
98	    subprocess.run(
99	        [_cc(), "-std=c11", f"-I{_INCLUDE_DIR}", str(c_path), "-o", str(bin_path)],
100	        check=True,
101	    )
102	    subprocess.run([str(bin_path), str(out_path)], check=True)
103	    return out_path
104	
105	
106	def test_ctypes_size_matches_c(known_state_bin: Path) -> None:
107	    raw = known_state_bin.read_bytes()
108	    assert len(raw) == HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE
109	
110	
111	def test_ctypes_header_fields(known_state_bin: Path) -> None:
112	    s = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(known_state_bin.read_bytes())
113	    assert s.magic == HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC
114	    assert s.version == HYBRID_STATE_VERSION

116	    assert s.hart_id == 0

123	    for i in range(32):
124	        assert s.gpr[i] == 0x1000 + i

126

129	    s = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(known_state_bin.read_bytes())
130	    assert s.mstatus == 0xabcdef01
131	    assert s.mepc == 0xdeadbeef
132	    assert s.mtvec == 0x80000040
133	    assert s.mcause == 7
134	    assert s.mtval == 0x1234
135	    assert s.mscratch == 0x5678
136	    assert s.mcycle == 1000
137	    assert s.minstret == 500
138	
139

141	    s = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(known_state_bin.read_bytes())
142	    for i in range(HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM):

144	    for i in range(HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM):

149	    s = HybridStateV1.from_buffer_copy(known_state_bin.read_bytes())
150	    assert s.vstart == 0
151	    assert s.vtype == 0xda
152	    assert s.vl == 16

163	
164	
165	def test_validate_state_file_rejects_bad_magic(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
166	    bad = tmp_path / "bad.bin"

173	    bad = tmp_path / "short.bin"

---
name: reference-hybrid-unit-test-host-build
description: Fast host g++ build+run command for hybrid doctest unit tests (no container)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 170e2aea-625a-4764-89fa-e0722f44012b
---

The `verilator/tests/hybrid/*.test.cpp` doctest unit tests are header-only
(C++20 + ABI header) and run directly on the host - no podman/Verilator needed.
Build+run one with:

```sh
cd /home/nick/work/hybrid_sim
g++ -std=c++20 -I verilator/src -I verilator/tests/hybrid -I include \
    -I verilator/external/doctest/doctest \
    verilator/tests/hybrid/resume_driver.test.cpp -o /tmp/t && /tmp/t
```

`-I verilator/tests/hybrid` is only needed for tests that include the shared
`recording_bus.hpp` (e.g. state_drain). This is the fast RED/GREEN loop; the
canonical container/ctest path is only required for the e2e suite.

Exceptions that do NOT link on the host: `qemu_handback.test.cpp` (needs libfmt:

"""Python ctypes mirror of `include/hybrid/state_abi.h::hybrid_state_v1`.

The C ABI is the wire contract between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the
orchestrator. This module mirrors it in ctypes so the orchestrator can
read and validate state files written by either CPU model.

Field offsets and the total struct size are asserted at import time
against the constants codified in `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`.
If a future ABI change forgets to update one side, importing this
module fails loudly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import struct
from pathlib import Path

HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC: int = 0x42594841
HYBRID_STATE_VERSION: int = 1

HYBRID_FLAG_RV64: int = 1 << 0
HYBRID_FLAG_FP: int = 1 << 1
HYBRID_FLAG_V: int = 1 << 2

HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: int = 64
HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM: int = 16
HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM: int = 64


class HybridStateV1(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("magic", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("version", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("flags", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("hart_id", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("pc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("priv", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("gpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("fpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("mstatus", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mepc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtvec", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcause", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtval", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mscratch", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("medeleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mideleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mip", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mie", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcycle", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("minstret", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("satp", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("pmpcfg", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM),
        ("pmpaddr", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM),
        ("vstart", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vtype", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vl", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vlenb", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vreg", ctypes.c_uint8 * (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)),
        ("vxsat", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vxrm", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vcsr", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("reserved", ctypes.c_uint8 * 232),
    ]


HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE: int = ctypes.sizeof(HybridStateV1)


# Mirror state_abi_check.h. If any of these fire, the ctypes layout has
# drifted from C and the wire format would be silently mis-parsed.
def _check_layout() -> None:
    expected: dict[str, int] = {
        "magic": 0,
        "version": 4,
        "flags": 8,
        "hart_id": 12,
        "pc": 16,
        "priv": 24,
        "gpr": 32,
        "fpr": 288,
        "mstatus": 544,
        "mepc": 552,
        "mtvec": 560,
        "mcause": 568,
        "mtval": 576,
        "mscratch": 584,
        "medeleg": 592,
        "mideleg": 600,
        "mip": 608,
        "mie": 616,
        "mcycle": 624,
        "minstret": 632,
        "satp": 640,
        "pmpcfg": 648,
        "pmpaddr": 776,
        "vstart": 1288,
        "vtype": 1296,
        "vl": 1304,
        "vlenb": 1312,
        "vreg": 1320,
    }
    vreg_end = 1320 + 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX
    expected["vxsat"] = vreg_end
    expected["vxrm"] = vreg_end + 8
    expected["vcsr"] = vreg_end + 16
    expected["reserved"] = vreg_end + 24
    for name, want in expected.items():
        got = getattr(HybridStateV1, name).offset
        if got != want:
            raise AssertionError(
                f"hybrid_state_v1.{name} offset mismatch: C={want} ctypes={got}"
            )
    want_size = vreg_end + 256
    if HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE != want_size:
        raise AssertionError(
            f"sizeof(hybrid_state_v1) mismatch: "
            f"C={want_size} ctypes={HYBRID_STATE_V1_SIZE}"

"""Python ctypes mirror of `include/hybrid/state_abi.h::hybrid_state_v1`.

The C ABI is the wire contract between QEMU plugin, vsim, and the
orchestrator. This module mirrors it in ctypes so the orchestrator can
read and validate state files written by either CPU model.

Field offsets and the total struct size are asserted at import time
against the constants codified in `include/hybrid/state_abi_check.h`.
If a future ABI change forgets to update one side, importing this
module fails loudly.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ctypes
import struct
from pathlib import Path

HYBRID_STATE_MAGIC: int = 0x42594841
HYBRID_STATE_VERSION: int = 1

HYBRID_FLAG_RV64: int = 1 << 0
HYBRID_FLAG_FP: int = 1 << 1
HYBRID_FLAG_V: int = 1 << 2

HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: int = 64
HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM: int = 16
HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM: int = 64


class HybridStateV1(ctypes.Structure):
    _fields_ = [
        ("magic", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("version", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("flags", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("hart_id", ctypes.c_uint32),
        ("pc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("priv", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("gpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("fpr", ctypes.c_uint64 * 32),
        ("mstatus", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mepc", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtvec", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcause", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mtval", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mscratch", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("medeleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mideleg", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mip", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mie", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("mcycle", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("minstret", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("satp", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("pmpcfg", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_CFG_NUM),
        ("pmpaddr", ctypes.c_uint64 * HYBRID_PMP_ADDR_NUM),
        ("vstart", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vtype", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vl", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vlenb", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vreg", ctypes.c_uint8 * (32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX)),
        ("vxsat", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vxrm", ctypes.c_uint64),
        ("vcsr", ctypes.c_uint64),

        ("minstret_at_measure_start", ctypes.c_uint64),

    ]

# Mirror state_abi_check.h. If any of these fire, the ctypes layout has
# drifted from C and the wire format would be silently mis-parsed.
def _check_layout() -> None:
    expected: dict[str, int] = {
        "magic": 0,
        "version": 4,
        "flags": 8,
        "hart_id": 12,
        "pc": 16,
        "priv": 24,
        "gpr": 32,
        "fpr": 288,
        "mstatus": 544,
        "mepc": 552,
        "mtvec": 560,
        "mcause": 568,
        "mtval": 576,
        "mscratch": 584,
        "medeleg": 592,
        "mideleg": 600,
        "mip": 608,
        "mie": 616,
        "mcycle": 624,
        "minstret": 632,
        "satp": 640,
        "pmpcfg": 648,
        "pmpaddr": 776,
        "vstart": 1288,
        "vtype": 1296,
        "vl": 1304,
        "vlenb": 1312,
        "vreg": 1320,

    vreg_end = 1320 + 32 * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX

1	// IcountTrigger - F6 sibling of CsrTrigger. Counts retired insns and fires
2	// HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT once the per-hart counter reaches the configured target.
3	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus.
4	//
5	// Duck-types the CsrTrigger surface so HandoffController's template
6	// instantiates cleanly for either:
7	//
8	//   - lookup(pc) -> std::optional<CsrTriggerHit>
9	//   - empty() -> bool
10	//   - observe_commit() -> void  (icount-specific; HandoffController calls
11	//                                via if-constexpr requires-clause)
12	//
13	// `pc` is ignored: icount fires on counter alone, not at any specific PC.
14	// Multi-hart out of scope - the counter is a single uint64_t, sized for one
15	// hart per plan-validation contract.
16	
17	#pragma once
18	
19	#include "hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp"
20	#include "hybrid/insn_match.h"
21	
22	#include <cstdint>
23	#include <optional>
24	
25	namespace hybrid
26	{
27	
28	class IcountTrigger
29	{
30	public:
31	  explicit IcountTrigger(uint64_t target) : target_{target} {}
32	
33	  void observe_commit() noexcept { ++retired_; }
34	
35	  auto lookup(uint64_t /*pc*/) const -> std::optional<CsrTriggerHit>
36	  {
37	    if (target_ == 0 || retired_ < target_) return std::nullopt;
38	    return CsrTriggerHit{HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT, /*insn=*/0u};
39	  }
40	
41	  auto empty() const -> bool { return target_ == 0; }
42	
43	  auto target() const -> uint64_t { return target_; }
44	  auto retired() const -> uint64_t { return retired_; }
45	
46	private:
47	  uint64_t target_;
48	  uint64_t retired_ = 0;
49	};
50	
51	}  // namespace hybrid

- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

### F14 - vsim `MeasureStartSnapshot` observer

- Status: done. New header
  `verilator/src/hybrid/measure_start_snapshot.hpp` exports
  `MeasureStartSnapshot{K, bus}` and a sibling `NullObserver`. The class
  owns a DmiBus pointer and an internal retire counter; `observe_commit()`
  is a no-op until the K-th call, at which point it halts the hart via
  DMCONTROL, abstract-reads `mcycle`/`minstret`, then issues resumereq
  so the workload continues. K=0 short-circuits before any DMI traffic.
  Accessors: `snapshot_reached()`, `mcycle_at_measure_start()`,
  `minstret_at_measure_start()`. `HandoffController` is now
  template-parameterised on a second slot
  `template<typename Trigger, typename Observer = NullObserver>` with
  two deduction guides so every existing call site keeps its
  `<Trigger>` instantiation. New 3-arg ctor takes the observer.
  `on_retire` calls `observer_.observe_commit()` through the same
  `if constexpr (requires {...})` pattern that already gates the
  trigger's observer hook. Doctest
  `verilator/tests/hybrid/measure_start_snapshot.test.cpp` covers K=0
  silence, K=1 first-commit capture, K=N exact-boundary fire,
  no-re-capture invariant, and a halt+resume sequence assertion on the
  recorded DMI ops. Existing icount_trigger / handoff_controller /
  state_drain doctests all stay green (CTAD preserved).
- Type: structural (new code; behavior gated by F15 CLI wiring)

TESTS_LIB_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
TOP_ROOT=$(cd -- "$TESTS_LIB_DIR/../.." && pwd)

if [ -z "${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}" ] && [ -f "$TOP_ROOT/config.env" ]; then

  VSIM_BIN="${VSIM_BIN:-$TOP_ROOT/verilator/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium}"

    if [ ! -e "$f" ]; then
      echo "skip: $f not built; run 'source ./setup.sh' and 'make -C tests/fixtures'"
      exit 77
    fi
  done

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F2b RED->GREEN: `./hsim run --mode icount` must print the window cycle
# count -- the vsim mcycle delta over the measured window (vsim drain
# mcycle - QEMU drain mcycle, offset 624) -- so icount mode shows the
# cycle figure required by the 4-mode model.
#
# Manual TDD smoke test (one real QEMU+vsim icount round-trip on the
# markerless GEMM fixture); not wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)
HSIM="$ROOT/hsim"
ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf"

. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/log.sh"

[ -x "$HSIM" ] || fail "missing executable: $HSIM"
[ -f "$ELF" ]  || fail "missing fixture: $ELF (run ./hsim build)"

out=$(timeout 120 "$HSIM" run "$ELF" --mode icount \
        --qemu-icount 2000 --vsim-icount 1000 2>&1) \
  || { echo "$out"; fail "hsim run --mode icount did not exit 0"; }

n=$(echo "$out" | sed -nE 's/.*window_cycles[^0-9]*([0-9]+).*/\1/p' | head -1)
{ [ -n "$n" ] && [ "$n" -gt 0 ]; } \
  || { echo "$out"; fail "window_cycles not a positive integer (got '${n:-}')"; }

echo "[ok] icount mode printed window_cycles=$n"
echo "PASS test_icount_window_cycles"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# End-to-end roundtrip harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim -> QEMU 2.
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
13	#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
14	#   ROI_START       pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol
15	#                   in $VSIM_ELF.
16	#   ROI_END         pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-out PC, same forms.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# End-to-end roundtrip harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim -> QEMU 2.
#
# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
# fine with it.
#
# Env:
#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
#   EXPECT_RC       Final exit code to assert (default 0).
#   TRIGGER_MODE    csr | pc (default csr).
#   ROI_START       pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol
#                   in $VSIM_ELF.
#   ROI_END         pc mode REQUIRED. Switch-out PC, same forms.
#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
#   VSIM_BIN, VSIM_QEMU, VSIM_PLUGIN, VSIM_ELF, NM  override built paths.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/roi.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:?FIXTURE env var is required (e.g. FIXTURE=rt_c_hello)}"
EXPECT_RC="${EXPECT_RC:-0}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"
TRIGGER_MODE="${TRIGGER_MODE:-csr}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

NM="${NM:-${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:+$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}}"
NM="${NM:-riscv64-unknown-elf-nm}"

case "$TRIGGER_MODE" in
  csr) ;;
  pc)
    if ! command -v "$NM" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "skip[$FIXTURE pc]: nm not found at $NM"
      exit 77
    fi
    NM_OUT=$("$NM" --defined-only "$VSIM_ELF")
    # ROI_START / ROI_END (env, both required) name the two switch PCs:
    # each is a 0x address or a symbol in $VSIM_ELF.
    roi_resolve_pair "$NM_OUT" "$FIXTURE pc" || exit 1
    ;;
  *)
    echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: unknown TRIGGER_MODE=$TRIGGER_MODE (use csr|pc)"
    exit 1
    ;;
esac

# 128 MB matches the QEMU virt machine default; vsim uses the same size.
SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-e2e-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

PLUGIN_ARGS="outfile=$STATE_QEMU"
VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=()
if [ "$TRIGGER_MODE" = "pc" ]; then
  PLUGIN_ARGS="$PLUGIN_ARGS,enter_pc=0x$ENTER_PC"
  VSIM_TRIG_ARGS=(--hybrid-exit-pc "0x$EXIT_PC")
fi

# Optional ROI kanata logging: hsim sets KANATA_FILE (and optionally
# OBJDUMP_FILE) when the user passes --kanata. vsim's --kanata-roi auto-
# derives the window from the resume PC and the unique exit PC.
VSIM_KANATA_ARGS=()
if [ -n "${KANATA_FILE:-}" ]; then
  VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--kanata "$KANATA_FILE" --kanata-roi)
  if [ -n "${OBJDUMP_FILE:-}" ]; then
    VSIM_KANATA_ARGS+=(--objdump "$OBJDUMP_FILE")
  fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F15 RED -> GREEN: vsim accepts --vsim-warmup-icount K and the drained
# state file carries the F13 warmup-snapshot fields populated.
#
# This is the structural plumbing test for the warmup wave: every later
# mode-specific e2e (F17 csr / F18 pc / F19 icount) layers tighter
# assertions on top of this contract.
#
# Test steps:
#   1. Run QEMU 1 + plugin on rt_c_v_regs to drain the entry state file.
#   2. Run vsim with --resume-from-qemu + --vsim-warmup-icount 1000.
#   3. Assert vsim exited 200 (drain on csrwi 0x7C0,1) and produced a state.
#   4. Read mcycle_at_measure_start / minstret_at_measure_start from the
#      drained file; both must be > 0 (snapshot fired during the ROI).
#
# Manual TDD smoke -- not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_regs}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-1000}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Light gate: vsim --help must announce the new flag, otherwise the binary
# is older than this test. Fails fast with a useful diagnostic.
if ! "$VSIM_BIN" --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--vsim-warmup-icount'; then
  fail "F15: $VSIM_BIN --help does not mention --vsim-warmup-icount (rebuild vsim)"
fi
ok "vsim --help mentions --vsim-warmup-icount"

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 did not produce state file"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?

MC_MS=$(python3 -c "

# F15 RED -> GREEN: vsim accepts --vsim-warmup-icount K and the drained
# state file carries the F13 warmup-snapshot fields populated.
#
# This is the structural plumbing test for the warmup wave: every later
# mode-specific e2e (F17 csr / F18 pc / F19 icount) layers tighter
# assertions on top of this contract.
#
# Test steps:
#   1. Run QEMU 1 + plugin on rt_c_v_regs to drain the entry state file.
#   2. Run vsim with --resume-from-qemu + --vsim-warmup-icount 1000.
#   3. Assert vsim exited 200 (drain on csrwi 0x7C0,1) and produced a state.
#   4. Read mcycle_at_measure_start / minstret_at_measure_start from the
#      drained file; both must be > 0 (snapshot fired during the ROI).
#
# Manual TDD smoke -- not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_regs}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-1000}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Light gate: vsim --help must announce the new flag, otherwise the binary
# is older than this test. Fails fast with a useful diagnostic.
if ! "$VSIM_BIN" --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--vsim-warmup-icount'; then
  fail "F15: $VSIM_BIN --help does not mention --vsim-warmup-icount (rebuild vsim)"
fi
ok "vsim --help mentions --vsim-warmup-icount"

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 did not produce state file"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1

set -e

if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then

")

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F15 RED -> GREEN: vsim accepts --vsim-warmup-icount K and the drained
# state file carries the F13 warmup-snapshot fields populated.
#
# This is the structural plumbing test for the warmup wave: every later
# mode-specific e2e (F17 csr / F18 pc / F19 icount) layers tighter
# assertions on top of this contract.
#
# Test steps:
#   1. Run QEMU 1 + plugin on rt_c_v_regs to drain the entry state file.
#   2. Run vsim with --resume-from-qemu + --vsim-warmup-icount 1000.
#   3. Assert vsim exited 200 (drain on csrwi 0x7C0,1) and produced a state.
#   4. Read mcycle_at_measure_start / minstret_at_measure_start from the
#      drained file; both must be > 0 (snapshot fired during the ROI).
#
# Manual TDD smoke -- not auto-wired into scripts/run_e2e.sh.

set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/paths.sh"
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

FIXTURE="${FIXTURE:-rt_c_v_regs}"
WARMUP_K="${WARMUP_K:-1000}"
TIMEOUT="${TIMEOUT:-60}"

hybrid_resolve_paths

# Light gate: vsim --help must announce the new flag, otherwise the binary
# is older than this test. Fails fast with a useful diagnostic.
if ! "$VSIM_BIN" --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--vsim-warmup-icount'; then
  fail "F15: $VSIM_BIN --help does not mention --vsim-warmup-icount (rebuild vsim)"
fi
ok "vsim --help mentions --vsim-warmup-icount"

SHARED_SIZE=$((128 * 1024 * 1024))
SHARED_MEM=$(mktemp -p /dev/shm vsim-warmup-shared.XXXXXX)
STATE_QEMU=$(mktemp)
STATE_VSIM=$(mktemp)
SIM_LOG=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$SHARED_MEM" "$STATE_QEMU" "$STATE_VSIM" "$SIM_LOG"' EXIT
truncate -s "$SHARED_SIZE" "$SHARED_MEM"

set +e
"$VSIM_QEMU" \
  -object "memory-backend-file,id=mem,share=on,mem-path=$SHARED_MEM,size=$SHARED_SIZE" \
  -machine andes_ae350,memory-backend=mem \
  -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=512 \
  -nographic \
  -semihosting-config enable=on,target=native \
  -bios "$VSIM_ELF" \
  -plugin "$VSIM_PLUGIN,outfile=$STATE_QEMU" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
QEMU1_RC=$?
set -e

[ "$QEMU1_RC" -eq 200 ] || fail "QEMU 1 expected exit 200 on drain, got $QEMU1_RC"
[ -s "$STATE_QEMU" ]    || fail "QEMU 1 did not produce state file"

set +e
timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$VSIM_BIN" "$VSIM_ELF" \
  --resume-from-qemu "$STATE_QEMU" \
  --handoff-out "$STATE_VSIM" \
  --shared-mem-path "$SHARED_MEM" \
  --shared-mem-size "$SHARED_SIZE" \
  --shared-mem-base 0x00000000 \
  --vsim-warmup-icount "$WARMUP_K" >"$SIM_LOG" 2>&1
VSIM_RC=$?
set -e

if [ "$VSIM_RC" -ne 200 ]; then
  echo "--- sim log ---"
  cat "$SIM_LOG"
  fail "vsim expected exit 200, got $VSIM_RC"
fi
[ -s "$STATE_VSIM" ] || fail "vsim did not produce state file"

# Warmup snapshot fields land in the state file via F13's ABI extension.
# Offset = vcsr (1320 + 32*64 + 16 = 3384) + 8 = 3392 (mcycle_at_measure_start),
#          3400 (minstret_at_measure_start). Locked by state_abi_check.h.
MC_MS=$(python3 -c "
import struct, sys
with open('$STATE_VSIM', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(3392); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
")
MI_MS=$(python3 -c "
import struct, sys
with open('$STATE_VSIM', 'rb') as f:
    f.seek(3400); print(struct.unpack('<Q', f.read(8))[0])
")

echo "[warmup] mcycle_at_measure_start=$MC_MS minstret_at_measure_start=$MI_MS K=$WARMUP_K"

[ "$MC_MS" -gt 0 ] \
  || fail "mcycle_at_measure_start expected > 0 with K=$WARMUP_K, got $MC_MS"
[ "$MI_MS" -gt 0 ] \
  || fail "minstret_at_measure_start expected > 0 with K=$WARMUP_K, got $MI_MS"

ok "warmup snapshot present in drained state (K=$WARMUP_K)"
echo "PASS test_vsim_warmup_icount_arg"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI boundary resolution for pc-trigger mode.
#
# pc mode switches QEMU <-> vsim at two PCs: the ROI start (drain QEMU) and
# the ROI end (drain vsim). Either boundary may be named as a 0x-prefixed
# hex address (used verbatim) OR as a symbol present in the ELF (resolved
# against `nm --defined-only` output). This decouples the switch points from
# the workload source: any function can be the ROI, with no planted markers.

# resolve_pc <boundary> <nm_output>
#   <boundary>  : "0x<hex>" | "0X<hex>" | symbol name
#   <nm_output> : `nm --defined-only` listing ("addr type name" per line)
# Prints the bare hex address (no 0x) on stdout, or nothing if a symbol name
# is not found (the caller treats empty as a fatal "cannot resolve").
resolve_pc() {
  local boundary="$1" nm_out="$2"
  case "$boundary" in
    0x*|0X*) printf '%s\n' "${boundary#0[xX]}" ;;
    *)       printf '%s\n' "$nm_out" | awk -v s="$boundary" '$3==s{print $1; exit}' ;;
  esac
}

# roi_resolve_pair <nm_output> [<label>]
#   Reads ROI_START / ROI_END from the environment (both REQUIRED), resolves
#   each against <nm_output>, and sets the globals ENTER_PC / EXIT_PC (bare
#   hex). Returns 1 and prints a FAIL line naming the offending boundary if
#   either is unset or does not resolve. <label> tags the FAIL message.
roi_resolve_pair() {
  local nm_out="$1" label="${2:-pc}"
  local start="${ROI_START:-}"
  local end="${ROI_END:-}"
  if [ -z "$start" ] || [ -z "$end" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: ROI_START and ROI_END must both be set (0x address or symbol name)"
    return 1
  fi
  ENTER_PC=$(resolve_pc "$start" "$nm_out")
  EXIT_PC=$(resolve_pc "$end" "$nm_out")
  if [ -z "$ENTER_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI start '$start' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  if [ -z "$EXIT_PC" ]; then
    echo "FAIL[$label]: cannot resolve ROI end '$end' (not a 0x address or a defined symbol)"
    return 1
  fi
  return 0
}
